title: Session lifecycle chronicle + API sketch
content:
Quick context / purpose:
This is a personal design journal for the session lifecycle surface we keep iterating on. Goal is to collect one place of heuristics + API shape + config knobs we can prototype in the runtime. Not a final product spec — intentionally rough.

Top-level goals:
- Make session creation/rehydration cheap (latency + cost) for common app patterns (chat, document context, tool-augmented flows).
- Provide explicit API for: create, snapshot, prewarm/prefetch, evict, transfer, and graceful-degrade.
- Keep server runtime state <= small per-session working set; allow session offload to blob store with compact manifest.
- Allow client-driven hints (priority, expected-turns, critical-prefix) to guide caching/batching.

Sketch: session resource model (conceptual)
- session_id: opaque string (client or server minted)
- live_state: in-memory KV (short lived, contains KV-cache pointers, last-active timestamp, partial KV shards)
- manifest: compact JSON blob stored in blobstore (s3/gs) with traces to recreate in-memory state (token count, compressed prefix cache keys, model variant used, quantization tag)
- lease: short TTL associated with live_state (default 30s), can be extended by keepalive or by runtime heuristics

API shapes (rough) - REST fragments and intent
1) Create session
POST /v1/sessions
Request body (client):
{
  "client_hint": {
    "expected_turns": 8,
    "priority": "hot",   // hot|warm|cold  (client hint, server may override)
    "critical_prefix": "system: user:onboarding-v2"
  },
  "model": "redwood-3b:v2",
  "pinned_configs": ["small-kv","fp16-kernel"]
}
Response: 201 + { session_id, created_at, lease_expires }
Notes: creation should optionally return a prewarm slot id when client requested immediate low-latency path.

2) Snapshot / checkpoint session
PUT /v1/sessions/:id/snapshot
Body: { "reason": "pause-save", "tags": ["handoff:mobile"], "preserve_in_memory": false }
Response: { snapshot_id, manifest_url }
Behavior: runtime compacts prefix caches and writes manifest; if preserve_in_memory=true keep live_state and extend lease.

3) Prefetch / prewarm (client initiated)
POST /v1/sessions/:id/prewarm
Body: { "type": "kv-prefix", "keys": ["user:123:recent_msgs"], "ttl": 120 }
Response: { ticket_id, expected_ready_at }
Notes: prewarm is a best-effort background op; ticket used to query readiness and cancel. Runtime may collapse similar prewarm requests.

4) Eviction / graceful degrade (admin or runtime triggered)
POST /v1/sessions/:id/evict
Body: { "mode": "snapshot-and-evict" }
Response: { evicted: true, manifest_url }
Behavior: preferred path is snapshot->release live memory but keep manifest. For critical sessions (priority=hot) we try attrition (reduce KV retention) before snapshot+evict.

Minimal manifest sketch (stringified JSON for storage)
{
  \"session_id\": \"...\",
  \"model\": \"redwood-3b:v2\",
  \"created_at\": \"2025-11-05T16:22:00Z\",
  \"prefix_cache_index\": [\"k1\", \"k2\"],
  \"kv_shards\": [\"s3://.../shard-1.bin\"],
  \"approx_tokens\": 1342
}

Runtime heuristics (brainstorm)
- Lease autoprolong: if request rate > X req/min for session extend lease; if background prewarm job present extend until job completes.
- Hot/warm cutoff: hot if expected_turns >= 4 and recent reqs within last 5m. Warm if expected_turns 1-3. Cold otherwise.
- Prefetch budget: per-tenant budget for prefetch; prefetches use a scoring function: score = weight_recency*recency + weight_priority*priority_score - cost_estimate. Evict low-score first.
- Adaptive snapshot frequency: for sessions with stable prefix (no new prefix writes) and > Y tokens, snapshot every N minutes.

ASCII diagram: request flow for handoff between clients (mobile -> web)

Client A (mobile)    -> LB -> routing -> runtime-A (has live_state)
    |                        |                      |
    | creates snapshot ->    | write manifest ---> blobstore
    |                        |                      |
Client B (web)    -> LB -> routing -> runtime-B (cold)
    |  GET /v1/sessions/:id/rehydrate?fast=true     |
    |  if manifest ready then start prewarm ticket ----> runtime-B launches kv fetch & small warmup
    |  response: 200 + { session_id, warmup_ticket }

Notes on fast vs safe rehydrate:
- fast: lazy streaming of KV shards (start accepting requests after minimal prefix available)
- safe: block until full manifest downloaded and KV checksums verified.
Tradeoffs: fast reduces tail latency at cost of some early errors if missing keys; safe increases cold-start but more deterministic outputs.

Edge cases / open questions (TODOs)
- How to represent incremental prefix deltas efficiently in manifest? Do we keep a write-ahead log per session or rebuild from last stable snapshot?
- Can we use model KV compression (e.g., Bloom filters) to avoid retrieving full shards on rehydrate?
- RBAC: manifest URLs are sensitive — should be signed short URLs per tenant + audit log.
- Cross-region rehydrates: serve from nearest blobstore replica; but what if model affinity requires a different region GPU? Add routing policy that includes model-host-region preference.

Observability / tracing ideas
- Each session lifecycle op emits an event: session.create, prewarm.schedule, prewarm.done, snapshot.write, evict, rehydrate.start, rehydrate.ready. Use these to compute cold-start latency, prewarm hit rates, and snapshot churn.
- Add session-level metadata to per-request traces (session_id, session_priority, manifest_version).

Prototype plan (next steps)
- Implement minimal API endpoints (create, snapshot, prewarm, rehydrate) behind feature flag.
- Wire a tiny manifest writer using existing blobstore infra (reuse s3-client util).
- Add a prewarm worker that can accept ticket requests and populate small KV cache in runtime.
- Run A/B with chat prod-sim workload to measure tail P95 cold start with/without fast-rehydrate.

Quick hack notes (commands & tickets)
- local testing: node ./scripts/mock_session_writer.js --session test-abc --tokens 1200
- GH draft pr: serving-runtime#451 (see linked artifact)
- Jira epic: CORE-1723 (session lifecycle exploration)

Rough personal heuristics (why I prefer this flow)
- Clients know expected_turns and critical_prefix better than runtime — letting them provide hints reduces wasted prefetch.
- Manifest-first snapshot keeps runtime memory small and lets us scale the hot set independently from blobstore size.

Signed-off notes: this is intentionally fuzzy. Use as a seed for the more structured PRD.

End of journal entry.
